nodes.name: Sublocal
nodes.statement: (Leroy CH 3) A sublocal Y subset X is defined by a nucleus e_Y: O(X) rightarrow O(X), such that O(Y) = Im(e_Y) = \U in O(X) | e_Y(U) = U\. The corresponding embedding is i_X : O(Y) rightarrow O(X). i^*_X(V) = e_X(V), (i_X)_*(U) = U And every nucleus e on O(X) defines a sublocal Y of X by O(Y) = Im(e)
nodes.raw_latex:
(Leroy CH 3)
    \label{def:sublocal}
    
    
    
    A sublocal $Y \subset X$ is defined by a nucleus $e_Y: O(X) \rightarrow O(X)$, such that $O(Y) = Im(e_Y) = \{U \in O(X) | e_Y(U) = U\}$.
    The corresponding embedding is $i_X : O(Y) \rightarrow O(X)$. $i^*_X(V) = e_X(V)$, $(i_X)_*(U) = U$
    And every nucleus $e$ on $O(X)$ defines a sublocal $Y$ of $X$ by $O(Y) = Im(e)$

The corresponding embedding is i_X : O(Y) rightarrow O(X). i^*_X(V) = e_X(V), (i_X)_*(U) = U And every nucleus e on O(X) defines a sublocal Y of X by O(Y) = Im(e)

nodes.name: (1.8) Properties of Complements
nodes.statement: For any open sublocal V of E and any sublocal X of E, we have: \[V cup X = E iff E setminus V subset X\] \[V cap X = emptyset iff X subset E setminus V\] And thereby: \[(E - U = E - V) implies U = V\]
assumptions: For any open sublocal V of E and any sublocal X of E
conclusions: we have: \[V cup X = E iff E setminus V subset X\] \[V cap X = emptyset iff X subset E setminus V\] And thereby: \[(E - U = E - V) implies U = V\]
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{lem:properties_of_complements}
    
    
    
    For any open sublocal $V$ of $E$ and any sublocal $X$ of $E$, we have:
    \[V \cup X = E \iff E \setminus V subset X\]
    \[V \cap X = \emptyset \iff X \subset E \setminus V\]
    And thereby:
    \[(E - U = E - V) \implies U = V\]

nodes.name: Measure on Locales
nodes.statement: A measure on a local X is a map mu : O(X) to [0,infty) such that: item mu(emptyset) = 0 item U subset V implies mu(U) le mu(V) item mu(U cup V) = mu(U) + mu(V) - mu(V cap V) item For any increasingly filtered family V_i of open sublocals of X, we have: \[mu(bigcup V_i) = sup_i mu(V_i)\] this means: For all i and j there exists a k such that V_i cup V_j subset V_k bzw. V_i subset V_k and V_j subset V_k. (Leroy III.1.)
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:measure_on_locals}
     
    
    
    A measure on a local $X$ is a map $\mu : O(X) \to [0,\infty)$ such that:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\mu(\emptyset) = 0$
        \item $U \subset V \implies \mu(U) \le \mu(V)$
        \item $\mu(U \cup V) = \mu(U) + \mu(V) - \mu(V \cap V)$
        \item For any increasingly filtered family $V_i$ of open sublocals of $X$, we have:
        \[\mu(\bigcup V_i) = \sup_i \mu(V_i)\] this means:
        For all $i$ and $j$ there exists a $k$ such that $V_i \cup V_j \subset V_k$ bzw. $V_i \subset V_k$ and $V_j \subset V_k$.
    \end{enumerate}
    (Leroy III.1.)

nodes.clean_text: For any measure mu on a local X, the caratheodory extension is: \[mu(A) = inf \mu(U) | A subset U in O(X)\,~Ain X\]

nodes.name: Proptery 0 (Commutes with sup)

conclusions: (Leroy lemme 3.1) The caratheodory extension of a measure on a local commutes with unions of increasing families.

nodes.name: Caratheodory Extensions are monotonic
nodes.statement: The caratheodory extension is monotonic i.e. \[A le B implies mu(A) le mu(B)\]
conclusions: The caratheodory extension is monotonic i.e.
\[A le B implies mu(A) le mu(B)\]

nodes.name: Regular Local
nodes.statement: A local is regular, if for all open sublocals U of E, the open sublocals V such that Vbar subset U recover U.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:regular_local}
    
    
    
    A local is regular, if for all open sublocals $U$ of $E$, the open sublocals $V$ such that $V\bar \subset U$ recover $U$.
nodes.clean_text: A local is regular, if for all open sublocals U of E, the open sublocals V such that Vbar subset U recover U.
nodes.label: def:regular_local

nodes.name: Neighborhood
nodes.statement: A neighborhood of a sublocal A of X is an open sublocal V of X such that A le V.

nodes.name: strictly additve
nodes.statement: (Leroy theorem 3.3.1) For any measure on a local X, the caratheodory extension is strictly additive, i.e. mu (A cup B) = mu(A) + mu(B) - mu(A cap B).
conclusions: (Leroy theorem 3.3.1) For any measure on a local X, the caratheodory extension is strictly additive, i.e.
mu (A cup B) = mu(A) + mu(B) - mu(A cap B).
nodes.raw_latex:
(Leroy theorem 3.3.1)
    \label{prop:strictly_additive}
    
    
    
    For any measure on a local $X$, the caratheodory extension is
    strictly additive, i.e. $\mu (A \cup B) = \mu(A) + \mu(B) - \mu(A \cap B)$.
nodes.clean_text: (Leroy theorem 3.3.1) For any measure on a local X, the caratheodory extension is strictly additive, i.e. mu (A cup B) = mu(A) + mu(B) - mu(A cap B).
nodes.label: prop:strictly_additive

conclusions: Any measure on a good enough topological space X induces a measure on the corresponding local.
